pages.x: By 1789 France was bankrupt, partly from helping the Americans win their revolution, and after a bad harvest bread cost more than it had for decades. King Louis XVI called the Estates-General, an assembly of clergy, nobles and commoners, for the first time since 1614.

The commoners, the Third Estate, declared themselves a National Assembly. Locked out of their hall, on 20 June 1789 they met in a royal tennis court and swore not to part until France had a constitution.

On 14 July 1789, fearing the king's troops would crush them, a Paris crowd stormed the Bastille, a fortress prison, for its gunpowder. It held only seven prisoners. The governor's head was carried through the streets on a pike.
In August 1789 the Assembly swept away the privileges of the nobles and the Church and issued the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.
pages.fx: Men are born and remain free and equal in rights, it said. Olympe de Gouges answered with a Declaration of the Rights of Woman.

pages.x: In June 1791 the royal family fled Paris in disguise, but the king was recognised, from his face on the money, it is said, and stopped at Varennes. He never won back the people's trust. In 1792, at war with Austria and Prussia, France became a republic.
Louis XVI, now plain Citizen Louis Capet, was tried and guillotined on 21 January 1793. Marie Antoinette followed in October. There is no proof that she ever said 'let them eat cake'.

Facing war and revolt, the Committee of Public Safety, led by Maximilien Robespierre, ruled by fear. Thousands more died in prison or were killed without trial, until Robespierre himself went to the guillotine in July 1794.
The revolution's wars made a young Corsican general famous. In November 1799 Napoleon Bonaparte seized power in a coup and declared the revolution over. Five years later he crowned himself emperor.

The revolution ended the old order of king, nobles and Church in France and spread its ideas across Europe: citizens equal before the law, rights for all, the nation above the king. Its motto, liberty, equality, fraternity, and its tricolour flag are still those of France.
